finding.title: Add a schema-version floor guard for UserDatabase — onUpgrade has no path below v25

evidence.quote:
onUpgrade: (Migrator m, int from, int to) async {
        if (from < 25) {

finding.why: git log -p on user_database.dart shows onUpgrade previously handled `if (from < 3)` through `if (from < 23)`; commit 9612d7a0 deleted that whole range and its own diff changes the docstring from '...schemaVersion bumped to 12; all old migration steps deleted' to describing a second 'W3.19 rebuild' wipe-install boundary. Today onUpgrade only starts at `from < 25`. database_provider.dart opens UserDatabase directly via driftDatabase(name: dbName) with no version-floor check at all — unlike ContentDatabase, which SeedManager guards with an explicit version comparison plus atomic replace before Drift ever touches it. Any real device whose local user_database.db is still at a schemaVersion below 25 will, on next launch, run onUpgrade(from=<old>, to=32): none of the intervening table-rename/profileId/FK changes apply, but Drift still stamps PRAGMA user_version=32 afterward — the on-disk schema stays frozen at its old shape while every DAO assumes v32's shape, so the first query throws 'no such column'/'no such table', or silently misreads a same-named-but-differently-typed column. coding-standards.md states as a current fact (2026-07-02) that 'the user DB is at schemaVersion 32 with real on-device data and no server backup', which is exactly the population this gap would hit. What would confirm real-world exposure: crash telemetry for 'no such column'/'no such table' immediately post-update, or checking whether any distributed build ever shipped schemaVersion 2-24 to non-dev devices before the WS7/v25 bump.
finding.recommendation: Add a pre-open guard (mirroring SeedManager's pattern) that reads PRAGMA user_version via raw sqlite3 before handing the file to Drift; if it's below the lowest version this onUpgrade body actually handles, run a documented recovery path (backup + fresh onCreate) instead of letting Drift silently half-upgrade. Longer term, adopt DB-4's drift_schemas/ + migrateAndValidate tests so a future 'delete old migration steps' edit fails CI instead of shipping silently.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test opens a DB stamped with a low PRAGMA user_version (e.g. 2) and asserts the app either migrates it correctly through to 32 or safely detects-and-recovers — it must never end up with user_version=32 stamped over pre-v25 table shape.
database_provider.dart (or a new guard module) checks on-disk PRAGMA user_version against a documented MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION before opening via Drift.
DB-4's drift_schemas/ export + generated migration tests land so a future deletion of an `if (from < N)` block fails CI.
